links.outcome: Self-consistency of LLM answers across three repeated runs on T2D education MCQs
links.effect: Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar had self-consistency of 60.4%-91.7%, while other models were at or above 95%.
links.quote: but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models (≥95%)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy and self-consistency across question configurations simulating different user backgrounds
links.effect: Most models reached ≥95% accuracy on configurations 1 and 2, but all models degraded in accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3.
links.quote: All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3.

unlisted_practices: Expert panel validation (CDCES, MD, endocrinologist) of LLM-transformed benchmark questions and answers
Converting clinician-collected real-world patient Q&A pairs into multiple-choice benchmark items

screen.reason: The paper introduces DiaBench, a multiple-choice question benchmark derived from real-world patient questions, to evaluate the accuracy and consistency of several LLMs for T2D patient education. It does not test a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
